<main id="main"><section class="profile-intro profile-intro-miguel wrap"><div class="profile-media"><figure class="profile-photo "><img src="../../assets/people/miguel-luque-cutout.png" alt="Portrait of Miguel Ángel Luque Fernández"></figure><div class="profile-role-band"><span>Group lead</span><div class="profile-links" role="group" aria-label="Profiles and contact"><a class="profile-icon-link" href="https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6683-5164" aria-label="ORCID profile"><img src="../../assets/icons/orcid.svg" alt=""></a><a class="profile-icon-link" href="https://scholar.google.es/citations?user=lA11XToAAAAJ&amp;hl" aria-label="Google Scholar profile"><img src="../../assets/icons/google-scholar.svg" alt=""></a><a class="profile-icon-link" href="https://github.com/migariane" aria-label="GitHub profile"><img src="../../assets/icons/github.svg" alt=""></a><a class="profile-icon-link profile-icon-email" href="mailto:mluquefe@ugr.es" aria-label="Send email"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="3" y="5" width="18" height="14" rx="2"/><path d="m4 7 8 6 8-6"/></svg></a></div></div><div class="profile-credentials"><div class="profile-appointment"><p class="profile-position">Associate Professor of Biostatistics</p><ul class="profile-affiliations"><li>Department of Statistics and Operations Research, University of Granada</li></ul></div><div class="profile-appointment"><p class="profile-position">Honorary Associate Professor</p><ul class="profile-affiliations"><li>London School of Hygiene &amp; Tropical Medicine</li></ul></div></div></div><div><div class="profile-name" role="heading" aria-level="1">Miguel Ángel Luque Fernández</div><p class="profile-bio">He earned his PhD in Preventive Medicine (Epidemiology) and Public Health, with <em>Summa Cum Laude</em>, from the University of Granada and the Université Libre de Bruxelles. He also holds a BSc in Mathematics and Statistics from the Open University, an MSc in Biostatistics from the University of Newcastle, an MSc in Epidemiology from the Université Libre de Bruxelles, and a Master of Public Health from the University of Granada.</p><p class="profile-bio">Following his doctorate in 2010, he held postdoctoral fellowships at the University of Cape Town and Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, specialising in epidemiological methods and causal inference. Trained as an Epidemic Intelligence Officer, he has worked in field epidemiology with Médecins Sans Frontières and WHO-GOARN in Haiti and sub-Saharan Africa.</p><p class="profile-bio">His research lies at the intersection of causal inference, biostatistics and computational epidemiology, with a particular focus on observational data. He works on targeted learning and doubly robust estimation, as well as applications to socioeconomic inequalities and cancer survival.</p></div></section><div class="profile-related-surface"><svg class="profile-wave profile-wave-top" viewBox="0 0 1440 80" preserveAspectRatio="none" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M0 16 C280 16 420 32 700 48 C980 64 1170 64 1440 64 L1440 80 H0 Z"/></svg><section class="section wrap section-tight profile-related research-selector" data-research-selector data-research-default="research-complex-treatments" data-research-placement="end"><div class="section-heading"><div><h2>Related research areas</h2></div></div><div class="research-grid"><a class="research-choice" href="#research-complex-treatments" data-research-select aria-controls="research-complex-treatments">Complex treatments</a><a class="research-choice" href="#research-targeted-learning" data-research-select aria-controls="research-targeted-learning">Targeted learning</a><a class="research-choice" href="#research-conformal-inference" data-research-select aria-controls="research-conformal-inference">Conformal inference</a><a class="research-choice" href="#research-population-health" data-research-select aria-controls="research-population-health">Population health</a><div class="research-panels" data-research-panels><article class="research-area-detail" id="research-complex-treatments" data-research-panel role="region" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="research-complex-treatments-title"><div class="research-visual"><img src="../../assets/line-complex.svg?v=6" alt="" width="300" height="150" loading="lazy"></div><div class="research-area-copy"><h3 id="research-complex-treatments-title">Causal estimation with complex exposures</h3><div class="research-area-body"><p>Methods for estimating causal effects of treatments with multiple levels or complex exposures within the potential outcomes framework. We combine doubly robust estimation, cross-fitting and influence-function-based inference, including when nuisance models are estimated with machine learning. The <a href="../../index.html#software">Software</a> section includes the <code>tmleMulti</code> implementation.</p></div></div></article><article class="research-area-detail" id="research-targeted-learning" data-research-panel role="region" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="research-targeted-learning-title"><div class="research-visual"><img src="../../assets/line-targeted.svg?v=15" alt="" width="300" height="150" loading="lazy"></div><div class="research-area-copy"><h3 id="research-targeted-learning-title">Targeted learning &amp; semiparametric efficiency</h3><div class="research-area-body"><p>Methods that combine statistical learning with causal estimation, including targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE) and doubly robust approaches. Semiparametric efficiency theory, influence functions and the delta method provide a basis for inference and variance estimation.</p></div></div></article><article class="research-area-detail" id="research-conformal-inference" data-research-panel role="region" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="research-conformal-inference-title"><div class="research-visual"><img src="../../assets/line-conformal.svg?v=13" alt="" width="300" height="150" loading="lazy"></div><div class="research-area-copy"><h3 id="research-conformal-inference-title">Conformal inference for causal questions</h3><div class="research-area-body"><p>Conformal methods for quantifying uncertainty in causal estimands, including settings that use machine learning or have small samples. We investigate the assumptions and conditions under which finite-sample coverage can be guaranteed.</p></div></div></article><article class="research-area-detail" id="research-population-health" data-research-panel role="region" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="research-population-health-title"><div class="research-visual"><img src="../../assets/line-population.svg?v=5" alt="" width="300" height="150" loading="lazy"></div><div class="research-area-copy"><h3 id="research-population-health-title">Computational epidemiology &amp; inequalities in cancer</h3><div class="research-area-body"><p>Applications of causal inference and computational epidemiology to population health. Topics include socioeconomic inequalities in cancer outcomes, emergency presentation and cancer survival, and reproducible, data-adaptive estimation.</p></div></div></article></div></div></section><svg class="profile-wave profile-wave-end" viewBox="0 0 1440 80" preserveAspectRatio="none" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M0 64 C280 64 470 64 740 48 C1010 32 1160 16 1440 16 L1440 80 H0 Z"/></svg></div></main>
